subject: Delegated signing & offline manifest exchange for islanded clusters
messages:
From: Tom Bradley <tom.bradley@edgecloud.io>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@edgecloud.io
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Islanded cluster - delegated signing & manifest exchange

Hi Rishi,

Quick background: we manage a set of fully air-gapped EdgeCloud sites (no inbound network). Our operator teams need a secure, auditable way to accept signed images and apply rolling updates without exposing keys or making the operator hold root signing keys.

Can Redwood outline a delegated signing flow that supports:
- offline manifest exchange (operator pulls a signed manifest via USB)
- verifier on-site for artifact integrity (offline verification tool)
- delegated operator signatures with limited-scope ephemeral keys (operator acknowledges receipt)
- clear chain-of-custody audit records for compliance (SOC2 readiness)

Attached: a sample manifest we use (islanded-manifest-v3.json).

We'd like to review options tomorrow morning PT.

Thanks,
Tom Bradley
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer
EdgeCloud Technologies

---
Attachment: islanded-manifest-v3.json (application/json)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Tom Bradley <tom.bradley@edgecloud.io>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Islanded cluster - delegated signing & manifest exchange

Tom — thanks for the clear ask and the manifest. High level here, then I propose a short runbook we can iterate on in the call: 

1) Signed manifests: Redwood will sign image manifests with a long-lived origin key in our HSM. The manifest bundle includes checksums, model/image version, allowed target groups, and a canonical release timestamp.

2) Delegated acknowledgement tokens: for operator-level acknowledgement we provide a short-lived delegation certificate (X.509 or JWT) scoped to a specific manifest id and site id. We do not issue operator signing keys for image artifacts; operators sign an "acceptance record" that is itself signed by the delegated certificate and verified at ingest.

3) Offline verification tool: a small CLI binary (sha256-signed) operators run on the isolated host to validate the manifest signature, verify image checksums, and produce an acceptance record. The acceptance record format is deterministic and inspectable.

4) Chain-of-custody: acceptance records are stored locally with operator identity, USB serial, and timestamp. When media is returned to networked ops, Redwood ingest accepts acceptance records (signed by the delegated cert) and associates them into the audit trail.

5) Rollout windows: propose canary on 5% of racks for first wave, operator confirmation required for each step. We can provide a fallback manifest if verification fails.

I'll attach a draft operator-handbook and a suggested manifest layout before the call. Would 8:30am PT tomorrow work for a 30-min sync?

- Rishi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Bradley <tom.bradley@edgecloud.io>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@edgecloud.io
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 07:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Islanded cluster - delegated signing & manifest exchange

Rishi — 8:30am PT works. Couple of constraints to highlight ahead of the call so we can make time productive: 
- Operators cannot use any networked signing or remote key retrieval; delegation certs must be provisionable onto the USB media before it reaches site.
- The acceptance record must be verifiable offline (no OCSP calls), i.e., include the issuing CA chain and revocation metadata in the bundle.
- We need replay protection: if an attacker replays an old acceptance record, it must be detectable.

Also, for auditing, we will want: site operator ID, USB serial, manifest id, acceptance timestamp, and the thumbprint of the verification binary used.

Looking forward to the runbook.

Tom

Tom — short notes from our internal run-through and a proposed minimal flow we can confirm on the call: 

A) Pre-deployment (networked environment):
- Redwood signs canonical manifest (manifest-id + metadata). Manifest and signature packaged into manifest-v3.bundle (manifest + .sig + CA chain + revocation list snapshot).
- Delegation issuance: for each scheduled deployment window, ops requests a Delegation Token for a given site group. Token is short-lived (valid for the scheduled 72-hr window) and exported as a DER certificate.

B) Media staging (airgap physical step):
- On staging machine, operator downloads: image blobs, manifest-v3.bundle, delegation certificate, offline verifier binary (sha256), and operator-handbook PDF. These are written to read-only media (signed at filesystem level where possible).
- Staging writes a manifest-index.txt with media serials and timestamps that the operator will sign upon receipt.

C) On-site (islanded):
- Operator runs offline verifier: checks bundle signature against embedded CA, runs image checksum verification, verifies delegation certificate validity window, and prompts operator to confirm site_id and USB serial.
- Verifier produces acceptance-record.json and signs it with the delegation certificate's private key (stored only on the staging machine, never on-site). Wait — note: since operator cannot hold signing keys on site, our flow uses the operator to produce a hardware-backed HMAC of the media serial (operator confirmation) and the staging machine produces the delegated attestation using its ephemeral key. The acceptance-record is bound to the USB serial and operator ID.

D) Return & ingest:
- Media returns to networked ops, acceptance-record and manifest bundle are uploaded to Redwood ingest. Redwood verifies the delegated attestation against the issuance log and records chain-of-custody.

We will propose a small change to ensure replay protection: include a monotonic nonce embedded in the manifest bundle that is unique per media write and checked at ingest time.

Will cover this on the call and show a mock run of the verifier binary. 30 minutes should be sufficient.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Islanded cluster - delegated signing & manifest exchange

Tom — thanks for the sync earlier. Per our notes, here's the agreed minimal acceptance flow and next steps. Please treat this as the canonical thread for audit trace: 

Agreed minimal flow (summary):
1) Redwood signs and publishes manifest-v3.bundle (manifest + signature + CA chain + revocation snapshot + nonce).
2) Ops schedules a deployment window and requests Delegation Token for site/hardware group. Token issued to staging account and exported to media.
3) Staging writes media (image blobs + manifest-v3.bundle + offline verifier binary + operator-handbook + manifest-index.txt). The staging machine produces a delegation-attestation.sig binding the manifest id, media serial, and delegation token id.
4) On-site operator runs verifier binary: verifies manifest signature, verifies delegation token validity (embedded), confirms site_id and USB serial, follows checklist in operator-handbook, and records operator confirmation values.
5) The staged delegation-attestation (signed by staging ephemeral key) and operator confirmation data travel back with the media; Redwood ingest verifies attestation, checks nonce against issuance log, and records chain-of-custody. Replay is prevented by the per-media nonce and by accepting only the first accepted attestation per media serial + manifest id.

Deliverables we will provide by end of week:
- verifier binary tarball + sha256 (signed)
- updated operator-handbook PDF (axioms + checklist)
- manifest schema v3 spec and example bundle
- ingest verification service endpoint and sample curl commands for ops to use post-return

Open items / action owners: 
- Karthik to create a short JIRA for the verifier CI job and packaging (SUP-877).
- Vanessa to share the mocked verifier demo and the manifest schema draft.
- Rishi to circulate the final acceptance checklist and audit mapping.

Thanks again — we logged this thread under Deal EC-REDWOOD-2028-Q2-17 for tracking.

- Rishi
